row_statement: Conjecture 2 of Choi and Needleman (if diam(C) > 1, diam(P) = 4 and r(P) = 3 then the uniform central appendage number A_ucg(C,P) equals 6) is false: for C the path on three vertices and an explicit connected 12-vertex graph P with diameter 4 and radius 3 there is a 20-vertex uniform central graph whose centre induces C, whose common eccentric set induces P, and which has five further vertices, so A_ucg(C,P) <= 5.

caveats: The source's own Theorem 4.1 already shows the value is 5 exactly when a covering number of P equals 2; the content here is the example, found by a SAT search. The journal (p. 178) says only that the authors had not found such a P.
The source states no tested range, so 'outside the tested range' cannot be shown; minimality of the witness is not proved.

A naive random search finds a smaller counterexample (P on 10 vertices, 11 edges) in 13 seconds, so the 12-vertex P is not minimal and the search was not hard; the authors' own search was evidently light.
